subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following temperature ranges is defined as the 'Danger Zone' by the USDA, where bacteria multiply most rapidly in food?
questions.explain: The USDA defines the Temperature Danger Zone as 40°F to 140°F, where bacteria grow most rapidly. (Note: Food service standards like ServSafe may use 41°F–135°F, but general nutrition texts used in HOSA often cite the USDA consumer standard).
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient arrives at the clinic with symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea 12–72 hours after attending a barbecue. The symptoms are most likely caused by **Salmonella**. Which food was the probable vector?
questions.explain: Salmonella is most commonly associated with raw or undercooked poultry and eggs. Canned goods are associated with Botulism; spinach with E. coli; rice with Bacillus cereus.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which internal temperature must poultry (such as chicken or turkey) reach to be considered safe for consumption?
questions.explain: According to USDA and HOSA guidelines, poultry must be cooked to an internal temperature of 165°F to kill Salmonella and Campylobacter.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A clinical dietitian is educating a patient with **Celiac disease**. Which of the following grains must the patient strictly avoid?
questions.explain: Celiac disease requires the avoidance of gluten, found in wheat, barley, and rye. Quinoa, rice, and corn are naturally gluten-free.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Distinguishing between a food allergy and a food intolerance is critical. Which of the following best describes the physiological mechanism of a **food allergy**?
options: The body lacks a specific enzyme to digest the food
The immune system produces IgE antibodies against a food protein
The digestive tract becomes irritated by acidic compounds
Bacteria in the gut ferment the food causing gas
questions.explain: A food allergy involves the immune system (specifically IgE antibodies) reacting to a protein. Intolerances (like lactose intolerance) are usually enzymatic deficiencies or digestive sensitivities.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which pathogen is notoriously associated with **improperly canned foods** (especially home-canned vegetables) and can cause paralysis or death?
questions.explain: Clostridium botulinum is an anaerobic bacterium that produces a neurotoxin in low-oxygen environments like improperly canned foods. It causes botulism.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A food handler has an open cut on their finger and does not wear a glove while preparing potato salad. Several hours later, customers report rapid onset of vomiting (within 1–6 hours). The likely pathogen is:
questions.explain: Staphylococcus aureus is found on human skin and in nasal passages. It produces a heat-stable toxin that causes rapid vomiting. It is a classic sign of poor personal hygiene/handling.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following describes the correct emergency treatment for a patient exhibiting signs of anaphylaxis (swelling of throat, difficulty breathing)?
options: Administer oral antihistamines and wait 30 minutes
Offer small sips of water to clear the throat
questions.explain: Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening medical emergency requiring immediate administration of epinephrine to reverse airway constriction and hypotension.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which population is at the highest risk for severe complications from **Listeria monocytogenes**, and which food should they avoid?
options: Pregnant women; unheated deli meats and soft cheeses
questions.explain: Listeria can cross the placenta and cause miscarriage or stillbirth. Pregnant women are advised to avoid soft cheeses (brie, feta) and cold deli meats unless heated to steaming.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Ground beef poses a unique risk for *E. coli* O157:H7 compared to whole steaks because:
options: Ground beef is harvested from a different animal
Surface bacteria are mixed into the center of the meat during grinding
Ground beef has a lower water content
Whole steaks are cooked to higher temperatures
questions.explain: Bacteria live on the surface of meat. Grinding distributes surface bacteria throughout the interior, necessitating a higher cooking temperature (155°F) compared to whole cuts (145°F).
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which enzyme is deficient in a patient with **lactose intolerance**?
questions.explain: Lactose intolerance is caused by a deficiency in lactase, the enzyme required to break down lactose (milk sugar) in the small intestine.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: The minimal internal safe cooking temperature for ground beef is:
questions.explain: Ground meats (beef, pork) must be cooked to 155°F (for 17 seconds) to ensure safety. Poultry is 165°F; whole cuts are 145°F.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: **Hemorrhagic colitis** and **Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)** are severe complications associated with which foodborne pathogen?
questions.explain: Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC), such as O157:H7, can cause bloody diarrhea (hemorrhagic colitis) and kidney failure (HUS), particularly in children.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following is the **safest** method for thawing a frozen turkey?
options: Leaving it on the kitchen counter overnight
Thawing in the refrigerator on the bottom shelf
questions.explain: Thawing in the refrigerator keeps the bird out of the Danger Zone (40°F-140°F). Thawing on the counter allows dormant bacteria to multiply rapidly as the outer layers warm up.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A food worker diagnosed with **Hepatitis A** or **Norovirus** must be:
options: Allowed to work if they wear double gloves
Excluded from the food operation until medically cleared
Allowed to work if asymptomatic for 12 hours
questions.explain: Hepatitis A and Norovirus are highly contagious and spread via the fecal-oral route. Infected workers must be excluded from the operation to prevent an outbreak.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Cross-contamination refers to:
options: Cooking different foods at different temperatures
The transfer of pathogens from one food/surface to another
Cleaning surfaces with soap but not sanitizer
Storing food in the refrigerator for too long
questions.explain: Cross-contamination occurs when pathogens are transferred from raw food (like chicken) to ready-to-eat food (like lettuce) via hands, cutting boards, or utensils.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following foods is one of the **Big 9** major food allergens regulated in the US?
questions.explain: The major allergens are Milk, Eggs, Fish, Shellfish, Tree Nuts, Peanuts, Wheat, Soy, and Sesame. Corn and strawberries are not classified as major allergens under current US labeling laws.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Infants under one year of age should not be fed honey because of the risk of:
questions.explain: Honey can contain Clostridium botulinum spores. While harmless to adults/older children, an infant's digestive system allows the spores to grow and produce toxins.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: When properly washing hands, the total time spent should be at least 20 seconds, with vigorous scrubbing taking up at least:
questions.explain: Proper handwashing involves wetting hands, applying soap, and scrubbing for 10-15 seconds, followed by rinsing and drying, for a total process of ~20 seconds.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: What is the primary danger of leaving cooked rice at room temperature for an extended period?
questions.explain: Cooked rice is prone to *Bacillus cereus*, a spore-forming bacterium that survives cooking. If left at room temp, spores germinate and produce a toxin causing 'Fried Rice Syndrome'.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: In a clinical setting, a 'gluten-free' label guarantees that the food contains less than which concentration of gluten?
questions.explain: FDA regulations allow the 'gluten-free' label on foods with less than 20 ppm of gluten, the level consistently shown to be safe for most people with Celiac disease.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following symptoms is unique to **Botulism** compared to other common foodborne illnesses?
questions.explain: Botulism neurotoxins cause descending paralysis, starting with cranial nerves. Early symptoms include diplopia (double vision), dysphagia (difficulty swallowing), and ptosis (drooping eyelids).
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: To prevent parasitic infection from **Trichinella spiralis**, which food was historically the primary concern, requiring thorough cooking?
questions.explain: Trichinosis is caused by parasitic roundworms found in undercooked pork (and game meats like bear). Modern farming has reduced this risk, but pork safety remains the classic context.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: An older adult in a nursing home is immunocompromised. Which of the following items should be removed from their menu to ensure food safety?
questions.explain: Raw sprouts (alfalfa, bean) pose a high risk for Salmonella and E. coli because the warm, humid conditions required for sprouting are ideal for bacterial growth. They are contraindicated for vulnerable populations.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition
